description:
The INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension (Rural) scheme was launched by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in the year 2007. 

This initiative is part of the broader INDIRAMMA program aimed at improving the living standards of marginalized communities in rural areas. 

The primary objective of the INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension scheme is to provide financial assistance to weavers who are aged 60 years and above. 

The scheme aims to ensure a sustainable livelihood for elderly weavers by providing them with a monthly pension. 

The pension amount is set at ₹1,500 per month. 

This financial support is intended to alleviate poverty and improve the quality of life for elderly weavers in rural areas. 

The scheme specifically targets weavers who belong to the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. 

To be eligible for the pension, applicants must be at least 60 years old. 

Additionally, they must have been engaged in weaving for a minimum of five years. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at ₹10,000 per month for the entire family. 

This income criterion ensures that the benefits reach those who are genuinely in need of financial assistance. 

The application process for the INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must submit their applications to the Mandal Revenue Officer. 

The application must include proof of age, which can be established through documents such as a birth certificate or an Aadhaar card. 

Weavers must also provide documentation that verifies their weaving profession. 

This could include a certificate from a recognized weaving society or cooperative. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the Mandal Revenue Officer for verification. 

The verification process typically takes about 30 days. 

If approved, the pension is disbursed directly into the bank account of the beneficiary. 

Pensions are disbursed on a monthly basis. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Handlooms and Textiles in Andhra Pradesh. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the application process and ensuring that the funds are disbursed to eligible beneficiaries. 

For any inquiries, beneficiaries can contact the Department of Handlooms and Textiles at their official office located in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh. 

The contact number for the department is 0866-2470000. 

The INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension scheme is a significant step towards social security for the weaver community. 

As of 2023, the scheme has benefited thousands of weavers across the state. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2023-2024. 

This allocation reflects the government's commitment to supporting the weaving community. 

The pension amount is reviewed periodically to ensure it remains relevant to the cost of living. 

In 2022, the government increased the pension from ₹1,000 to ₹1,500 to address inflation and rising living costs. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in reducing the economic vulnerability of elderly weavers. 

According to the latest statistics, approximately 50,000 weavers are currently receiving benefits under this scheme. 

The government aims to increase this number by reaching out to more eligible beneficiaries. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted regularly to inform weavers about the scheme and its benefits. 

These campaigns are carried out in collaboration with local self-help groups and community organizations. 

The INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare schemes aimed at empowering marginalized communities. 

Other related schemes include the Weavers Credit Card Scheme and the Handloom Weavers Comprehensive Welfare Scheme. 

These initiatives collectively aim to enhance the livelihood opportunities for weavers and their families. 

The government also provides skill development programs to help weavers adapt to changing market demands. 

These programs are designed to improve the quality of handloom products and increase competitiveness. 

The INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries. 

Many elderly weavers have expressed gratitude for the financial support that helps them meet their daily needs. 

The scheme has also contributed to the social dignity of weavers by recognizing their contributions to the textile industry. 

The government continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme to ensure transparency and efficiency. 

Regular audits are conducted to assess the utilization of funds and the impact of the scheme on beneficiaries. 

The INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension scheme is a vital component of the social welfare landscape in Andhra Pradesh. 

It exemplifies the government's commitment to uplifting the lives of vulnerable populations. 

The scheme not only provides financial assistance but also fosters a sense of community among weavers. 

By supporting elderly weavers, the government is preserving traditional weaving practices and cultural heritage. 

In conclusion, the INDIRAMMA Weavers Pension (Rural) scheme is a comprehensive initiative designed to support elderly weavers in Andhra Pradesh. 

With a monthly pension of ₹1,500 and a focus on marginalized communities, the scheme aims to improve the quality of life for its beneficiaries. 

The application process is accessible, and the government is committed to expanding the reach of the scheme. 

Through this initiative, the government seeks to empower weavers and ensure their economic security in their later years.
